audit.whatIsWrong: The content chart contradicted five of its own seven why-strings. It gave Gragas levels 2 and 3 where whys[1] says 'Wukong wins the early point-blank trade' and whys[2] calls level 3 'his cleanest all-in window'; it gave Skill at 4-5 and 6 where whys[3] says you win the extended trades and whys[4] calls the level-6 combo 'a real kill combo'; and it gave Gragas at two-plus items where whys[6] says 'Full-build Wukong out-duels you'.
audit.why: packet.levelChart reads Skill / Wukong / Wukong / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas / Wukong, which is exactly what the prose on both layers describes. Win rate 50.73% over 546 games — an even lane with an owner-favoured middle.
audit.corrected: Both charts flipped as one atomic group to Skill / Wukong / Wukong / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas / Wukong, with ratings adjusted.

audit.why: spikes[] already names the right four windows — his levels 1-2 Crushing Blow edge, his level 3 all-in, your Riftmaker peak, and his two-item reclaim. Only the chart sides were wrong, and the full-layer phase ratings followed them.
audit.corrected: Chart sides and ratings realigned to those spikes; no spike text needed changing.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer contained no ability interaction at all — 'His escape. Burst when it's down.', 'Your committal tool', 'Your ultimate'. The decisive one, that Body Slam collides with the first enemy unit it meets and so is eaten outright by a Warrior Trickster decoy, was never stated.
audit.why: Riot's text for Gragas E: 'Gragas charges to a location and collides with the first enemy unit he comes across' — 600 range, 14s at rank 1. That is precisely why a decoy is a free 14 seconds for Wukong.
audit.corrected: Written into tradeBad, dosFull[1], dontsFull[0], dontsFull[2], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5], using only Gragas-side numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried placeholders and no named ability behaviour.
audit.why: Nimbus Strike being both his entry and his exit, and Warrior Trickster eating a committal cooldown, are the two windows that decide when Gragas can spend E or R.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wukong's W was written as 'Warrior's Trickster' in whys[6], spikes[3].text and the late paragraph.
audit.why: packet.enemyAbilities gives the real name as Warrior Trickster, with no possessive. This is the one genuine name defect in the matchup.
audit.corrected: All three occurrences corrected to Warrior Trickster.

notes: IMPORTANT DATA GAP: the brief's enemyKit for Wukong is null, so no Riot ability text, cooldowns, ranges or costs were available for him. Every edit here is therefore grounded only in Gragas's own kit (Body Slam 600 range / 14s at rank 1, collides with the first unit) and in packet.enemyAbilities for names. No Wukong cooldown or range has been asserted anywhere. If the applier can regenerate this brief with a populated Wukong kit, the full layer would take a second, better pass. Of the three suspectNames, two are FALSE POSITIVES ('Use Drunken Rage', 'Use Explosive Cask' — the matcher caught the verb) and one is REAL: 'Warrior's Trickster' should be Warrior Trickster, fixed in three places.
